Core Active Vocabulary (5 items):

feel — to have a physical or emotional state. Example: I feel tired today.
sick — not well, ill. Example: I feel sick.
tired — needing rest or sleep. Example: She feels tired.
well — in good health. Example: I don't feel well.
healthy — in good health, or good for health. Example: She feels healthy.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• How do you feel?
• I feel ...
• I don't feel well.
• She feels sick.
• I feel healthy.

Grammar focus: Expressing pain with 'have got' / 'feel'.
Use feel + adjective: I feel tired. She feels sick. Negative: I don't feel well. Use healthy for good health and good habits.

Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
Today I feel tired and sick. I don't feel well. My sister feels healthy because she sleeps eight hours. My brother feels tired after work and he goes to bed early. I feel well today and I am happy.
